name: Vantablack Site Perimeter Tech Uniform
description: Worn by Vantablack's perimeter security and site surveillance personnel — the operational layer below full intelligence operatives — this uniform is deliberately understated. Flat charcoal trousers with reinforced knee panels pair with a close-cut long-sleeve duty shirt in the same tone. The fabric is a matte microfiber engineered to absorb ambient light at a higher rate than standard materials, reducing visual signature under low-light conditions without full stealth-tech coating. Chest pockets are sealed with magnetic closures, and the collar has an integrated signal-dampening layer that partially obscures BCI handshake emissions within a one-meter radius. No visible branding. A small Vantablack registry code is laser-etched inside the collar.
cultural_context: Vantablack uniforms are designed to be forgettable, and they largely succeed. Personnel in these uniforms occupy the background of corporate events, transit hubs, and high-tier building lobbies — present but unregistered in the mind. That invisibility is the point, and it makes them deeply unsettling to those who know what they're looking at.
story_hooks: A perimeter tech is found to have been wearing their uniform off-shift, conducting what appears to be unauthorized surveillance of a Tier 2 community organizer.
Someone is selling reproductions of the uniform at a gray market stall — the BCI dampening collar works, and it's attracting the wrong kind of buyers.
A player acquires one and discovers the registry code inside the collar is linked to a personnel file that officially doesn't exist.
